output.title: Rounding claims in a one-person business
output.body:
If you run a one-person business, the useful question is not whether AI can “handle claims.” It is whether the work is repeatable enough to become a bounded workflow instead of a fresh judgment call every time.

Use a simple decision rule: keep it manual when each case needs new context or an exception; consider support only when the same checks happen again and again. In that case, AI can sort, compare, or flag items before you review them. Final approval stays with you. Human-only approval and refusal of agent approval are demonstrated in Bareni’s self-built accounts-payable demo on synthetic data, but for a claims workflow this is still a design rule, not an existing deployed system.

A practical next step is to map one week of the current process. Write down the trigger, the inputs, the rule you use, where rounding happens, and where you stop to check by hand. Then mark which step is actually repeatable. If the rule can be written clearly, it may be worth supporting. If it depends on judgement every time, manual review is still the right default.

That is the filter: not “Can AI do it?” but “Which part is stable enough to standardise without giving up owner control?”
